Axis powers.question: Later, _____ mountain troops joined the German campaign in the Caucasus, reaching as far as Nalchik
Axis powers.fact: Romanian troops fought their way into the Crimea alongside German troops and contributed significantly to the Siege of Sevastopol. Later, Romanian mountain troops joined the German campaign in the Caucasus, reaching as far as Nalchik.

Axis powers.fact: The Romanian Navy also built sizable warships, such as the minelayer NMS Amiral Murgescu and the submarines NMS Rechinul and NMS Marsuinul.

Axis powers.fact: The country had built armored fighting vehicles as well, most notably the Mareșal tank destroyer, that likely influenced the design of the German Hetzer.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: Another British historian, Mark Axworthy, believes that Romania could even be considered to have had the second most important Axis army of Europe, even more so than that of Italy.

Axis powers.fact: Between 45,000 and 60,000 Jews were killed in Bukovina and Bessarabia by Romanian and German troops in 1941.

Axis powers.fact: According to Wilhelm Filderman at least 150,000 Jews of Bessarabia and Bukovina, died under the Antonescu regime (both those deported and those who remained).

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Overall, approximately 250,000 Jews under _____ jurisdiction died
Axis powers.fact: Between 45,000 and 60,000 Jews were killed in Bukovina and Bessarabia by Romanian and German troops in 1941. Overall, approximately 250,000 Jews under Romanian jurisdiction died.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: By 1943, the tide began to turn.

Axis powers.question: The Soviets pushed further west, retaking Ukraine and eventually launching an unsuccessful invasion of eastern Romania in the spring of _____
Axis powers.fact: The Soviets pushed further west, retaking Ukraine and eventually launching an unsuccessful invasion of eastern Romania in the spring of 1944. During the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive of August 1944, Romania switched sides on August 23, 1944.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: The Soviets pushed further west, retaking Ukraine and eventually launching an unsuccessful invasion of eastern Romania in the spring of 1944. During the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive of August 1944, Romania switched sides on August 23, 1944.

Axis powers.fact: Romanian troops then fought alongside the Soviet Army until the end of the war, reaching as far as Czechoslovakia and Austria.

Axis powers.question: After the September _____ Armistice of Cassibile with Italy, Romania became the second Axis power in Europe
Axis powers.fact: After the September 1943 Armistice of Cassibile with Italy, Romania became the second Axis power in Europe.

Axis powers.fact: The Romanians shared in the spoils of Operation Achse, Regia Marina's 5 CB-class midget submarines in the Black Sea being transferred to the Romanian Navy.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: Romania also captured 496 Italians, mostly naval personnel (2 of them later died).

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Before the month was out, _____ had agreed to systematically supply the Romanian Army with German military vehicles, via the Olivenbaum I-III and Quittenbaum I programs
Axis powers.fact: Before the month was out, Germany had agreed to systematically supply the Romanian Army with German military vehicles, via the Olivenbaum I-III and Quittenbaum I programs. Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: Deliveries started in November 1943, and by August 1944, Germany had supplied Romania with 10 times more armored vehicles (Panzer III, Panzer IV and Sturmgeschütz III) than during the entire pre-Cassibile period.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Having acquired the license to produce the _____ 109, Romania planned to assemble 75 from German parts
Axis powers.fact: Having acquired the license to produce the Messerschmitt Bf 109, Romania planned to assemble 75 from German parts.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Deliveries began in May _____, but only 6 were completed before Romania left the Axis in August 1944
Axis powers.fact: Deliveries started in November 1943, and by August 1944, Germany had supplied Romania with 10 times more armored vehicles (Panzer III, Panzer IV and Sturmgeschütz III) than during the entire pre-Cassibile period. Deliveries began in May 1944, but only 6 were completed before Romania left the Axis in August 1944.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: In _____, Romania had also gained access to certain Wunderwaffen, such as the Werfer-Granate 21
Axis powers.fact: Deliveries began in May 1944, but only 6 were completed before Romania left the Axis in August 1944. In 1944, Romania had also gained access to certain Wunderwaffen, such as the Werfer-Granate 21.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The first Romanian-made Fiesler Storch was completed in October _____, followed by 9 more by May 1944
Axis powers.fact: The first Romanian-made Fiesler Storch was completed in October 1943, followed by 9 more by May 1944. The 75 mm Reșița gun (production started at the end of 1943) used the projectile chamber of the German Pak 40.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: On 6 January _____, Antonescu showed Hitler the plans of the M-04 prototype of the Mareșal tank destroyer
Axis powers.fact: From March 1944, Germany also contributed to the design and construction of the M-05 and M-06 prototypes of the Mareșal tank destroyer: Alkett contributed to the Romanian design team and Telefunken radios along with Böhler armor were provided. On 6 January 1944, Antonescu showed Hitler the plans of the M-04 prototype of the Mareșal tank destroyer.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: In May _____, Lieutenant-Colonel Ventz from the Waffenamt acknowledged that the Hetzer had followed the Romanian design
Axis powers.fact: On 6 January 1944, Antonescu showed Hitler the plans of the M-04 prototype of the Mareșal tank destroyer. In May 1944, Lieutenant-Colonel Ventz from the Waffenamt acknowledged that the Hetzer had followed the Romanian design.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: German-led Army Group South Ukraine could not take major operational decisions without securing Ion Antonescu's approval, even as late as 22 August _____ (the day before he was dismissed)
Axis powers.fact: On 6 January 1944, Antonescu showed Hitler the plans of the M-04 prototype of the Mareșal tank destroyer. In May 1944, Lieutenant-Colonel Ventz from the Waffenamt acknowledged that the Hetzer had followed the Romanian design.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: An entire German army (the 6th) came under Romanian command in May _____, when it became part of Romanian general Petre Dumitrescu's Armeegruppe
Axis powers.fact: On 6 January 1944, Antonescu showed Hitler the plans of the M-04 prototype of the Mareșal tank destroyer. In May 1944, Lieutenant-Colonel Ventz from the Waffenamt acknowledged that the Hetzer had followed the Romanian design.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: For the first time in the war, _____ commanders came under the actual (rather than nominal) command of their foreign allies
Axis powers.fact: German-led Army Group South Ukraine could not take major operational decisions without securing Ion Antonescu's approval, even as late as 22 August 1944 (the day before he was dismissed). An entire German army (the 6th) came under Romanian command in May 1944, when it became part of Romanian general Petre Dumitrescu's Armeegruppe.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: Slovakia had been closely aligned with Germany almost immediately from its declaration of independence from Czechoslovakia on 14 March 1939. Slovakia entered into a treaty of protection with Germany on 23 March 1939.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: Slovakia had been closely aligned with Germany almost immediately from its declaration of independence from Czechoslovakia on 14 March 1939. Slovakia entered into a treaty of protection with Germany on 23 March 1939.

Axis powers.fact: This Romanian-led army group had 24 divisions of which 17 were German. Slovakia had been closely aligned with Germany almost immediately from its declaration of independence from Czechoslovakia on 14 March 1939.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Those two regions, along with Cieszyn Silesia, had been disputed between Poland and Czechoslovakia since _____
Axis powers.fact: Those two regions, along with Cieszyn Silesia, had been disputed between Poland and Czechoslovakia since 1918.

Axis powers.question: The Poles fully annexed them following the _____
Axis powers.fact: The Poles fully annexed them following the Munich Agreement.

Axis powers.question: After the invasion of _____, Slovakia reclaimed control of those territories
Axis powers.fact: Slovak troops joined the German invasion of Poland, having interest in Spiš and Orava. Those two regions, along with Cieszyn Silesia, had been disputed between Poland and Czechoslovakia since 1918.

Axis powers.fact: Those two regions, along with Cieszyn Silesia, had been disputed between Poland and Czechoslovakia since 1918. After the invasion of Poland, Slovakia reclaimed control of those territories.

Axis powers.question: Slovakia declared war on the Soviet Union in _____ and signed the revived Anti-Comintern Pact in 1941
Axis powers.fact: Slovakia declared war on the Soviet Union in 1941 and signed the revived Anti-Comintern Pact in 1941.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Slovak troops fought on _____'s Eastern Front, furnishing Germany with two divisions totaling 80,000 men
Axis powers.fact: Slovak troops fought on Germany's Eastern Front, furnishing Germany with two divisions totaling 80,000 men.

Axis powers.question: Slovakia declared war on the United Kingdom and the United States in _____
Axis powers.fact: Slovakia declared war on the United Kingdom and the United States in 1942.

Axis powers.question: Slovakia was spared German military occupation until the Slovak National Uprising, which began on 29 August _____, and was almost immediately crushed by the Waffen SS and Slovak troops loyal to Josef
Axis powers.fact: Slovakia was spared German military occupation until the Slovak National Uprising, which began on 29 August 1944, and was almost immediately crushed by the Waffen SS and Slovak troops loyal to Josef Tiso.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: After the war, Tiso was executed and _____ once again became part of Czechoslovakia
Axis powers.fact: Slovakia declared war on the United Kingdom and the United States in 1942. Slovakia was spared German military occupation until the Slovak National Uprising, which began on 29 August 1944, and was almost immediately crushed by the Waffen SS and Slovak troops loyal to Josef Tiso.

Axis powers.fact: During the 1930s, because of traditional right-wing elements, Bulgaria drew closer to Nazi Germany.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.fact: In 1940 Germany pressured Romania to sign the Treaty of Craiova, returning to Bulgaria the region of Southern Dobrudja, which it had lost in 1913.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The Germans also promised _____ – if it joined the Axis – an enlargement of its territory to the borders specified in the Treaty of San Stefano
Axis powers.fact: Bulgaria had been on the losing side in the First World War and sought a return of what the Bulgarian leadership saw as lost ethnically and historically Bulgarian territories, specifically in Macedonia and Thrace (divided between the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, the Kingdom of Greece, and Turkey). During the 1930s, because of traditional right-wing elements, Bulgaria drew closer to Nazi Germany.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Bulgaria participated in the Axis invasion of _____ and Greece by letting German troops attack from its territory and sent troops to Greece on April 20
Axis powers.fact: Bulgaria participated in the Axis invasion of Yugoslavia and Greece by letting German troops attack from its territory and sent troops to Greece on April 20. As a reward, the Axis powers allowed Bulgaria to occupy parts of both countries – southern and south-eastern Yugoslavia (Vardar Banovina) and north-eastern Greece (parts of Greek Macedonia and Greek Thrace).

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Despite German pressure, _____ did not take part in the Axis invasion of the Soviet Union and actually never declared war on the Soviet Union
Axis powers.fact: Bulgaria participated in the Axis invasion of Yugoslavia and Greece by letting German troops attack from its territory and sent troops to Greece on April 20. As a reward, the Axis powers allowed Bulgaria to occupy parts of both countries – southern and south-eastern Yugoslavia (Vardar Banovina) and north-eastern Greece (parts of Greek Macedonia and Greek Thrace).

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The Bulgarian Navy was nonetheless involved in a number of skirmishes with the _____, which attacked Bulgarian shipping
Axis powers.fact: The Bulgarian Navy was nonetheless involved in a number of skirmishes with the Soviet Black Sea Fleet, which attacked Bulgarian shipping.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Following the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in December _____, the Bulgarian government declared war on the Western Allies
Axis powers.fact: Following the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, the Bulgarian government declared war on the Western Allies.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: This turned into a disaster for the citizens of Sofia and other major Bulgarian cities, which were heavily bombed by the Allies in the winter of _____–1944
Axis powers.fact: This action remained largely symbolic (at least from the Bulgarian perspective), until August 1943, when Bulgarian air defense and air force attacked Allied bombers, returning (heavily damaged) from a mission over the Romanian oil refineries. This turned into a disaster for the citizens of Sofia and other major Bulgarian cities, which were heavily bombed by the Allies in the winter of 1943–1944.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: On 2 September _____, as the Red Army approached the Bulgarian border, a new Bulgarian government came to power and sought peace with the Allies, expelled the few remaining German troops, and declared
Axis powers.fact: This turned into a disaster for the citizens of Sofia and other major Bulgarian cities, which were heavily bombed by the Allies in the winter of 1943–1944. On 2 September 1944, as the Red Army approached the Bulgarian border, a new Bulgarian government came to power and sought peace with the Allies, expelled the few remaining German troops, and declared neutrality.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: This was followed by the coup d'état of 9 September _____, which brought a government of the pro-Soviet Fatherland Front to power
Axis powers.fact: This turned into a disaster for the citizens of Sofia and other major Bulgarian cities, which were heavily bombed by the Allies in the winter of 1943–1944. On 2 September 1944, as the Red Army approached the Bulgarian border, a new Bulgarian government came to power and sought peace with the Allies, expelled the few remaining German troops, and declared neutrality.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: These measures however did not prevent the _____ from declaring war on Bulgaria on 5 September, and on 8 September the Red Army marched into the country, meeting no resistance
Axis powers.fact: These measures however did not prevent the Soviet Union from declaring war on Bulgaria on 5 September, and on 8 September the Red Army marched into the country, meeting no resistance.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: After this, the _____ army (as part of the Red Army's 3rd Ukrainian Front) fought the Germans in Yugoslavia and Hungary, sustaining numerous casualties
Axis powers.fact: On 2 September 1944, as the Red Army approached the Bulgarian border, a new Bulgarian government came to power and sought peace with the Allies, expelled the few remaining German troops, and declared neutrality. After this, the Bulgarian army (as part of the Red Army's 3rd Ukrainian Front) fought the Germans in Yugoslavia and Hungary, sustaining numerous casualties.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Despite this, the _____ treated Bulgaria as one of the defeated countries
Axis powers.fact: Despite this, the Paris Peace Treaty treated Bulgaria as one of the defeated countries.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Bulgaria was allowed to keep _____, but had to give up all claims to Greek and Yugoslav territory
Axis powers.fact: Bulgaria was allowed to keep Southern Dobruja, but had to give up all claims to Greek and Yugoslav territory.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The NDH remained a member of the Axis until the end of _____, its forces fighting for Germany even after its territory had been overrun by Yugoslav Partisans
Axis powers.fact: The NDH remained a member of the Axis until the end of Second World War, its forces fighting for Germany even after its territory had been overrun by Yugoslav Partisans.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: On 16 April _____, Ante Pavelić, a Croatian nationalist and one of the founders of the Ustaše ("Croatian Liberation Movement"), was proclaimed Poglavnik (leader) of the new regime
Axis powers.fact: On 16 April 1941, Ante Pavelić, a Croatian nationalist and one of the founders of the Ustaše ("Croatian Liberation Movement"), was proclaimed Poglavnik (leader) of the new regime. Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: In _____ during the Italian invasion of Greece, Mussolini requested that Germany invade Yugoslavia to save the Italian forces in Greece
Axis powers.fact: On 16 April 1941, Ante Pavelić, a Croatian nationalist and one of the founders of the Ustaše ("Croatian Liberation Movement"), was proclaimed Poglavnik (leader) of the new regime. In 1941 during the Italian invasion of Greece, Mussolini requested that Germany invade Yugoslavia to save the Italian forces in Greece.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Initially the _____še had been heavily influenced by Italy
Axis powers.fact: On 16 April 1941, Ante Pavelić, a Croatian nationalist and one of the founders of the Ustaše ("Croatian Liberation Movement"), was proclaimed Poglavnik (leader) of the new regime. Initially the Ustaše had been heavily influenced by Italy.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Hitler reluctantly agreed; _____ was invaded and the NDH was created
Axis powers.fact: They were actively supported by Mussolini's National Fascist Party regime in Italy, which gave the movement training grounds to prepare for war against Yugoslavia, as well as accepting Pavelić as an exile and allowing him to reside in Rome. In 1941 during the Italian invasion of Greece, Mussolini requested that Germany invade Yugoslavia to save the Italian forces in Greece.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The next day, _____ć signed the Contracts of Rome with Mussolini, ceding Dalmatia to Italy and fixing the permanent borders between the NDH and Italy
Axis powers.fact: Pavelić led a delegation to Rome and offered the crown of the NDH to an Italian prince of the House of Savoy, who was crowned Tomislav II. The next day, Pavelić signed the Contracts of Rome with Mussolini, ceding Dalmatia to Italy and fixing the permanent borders between the NDH and Italy.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Italian armed forces were allowed to control all of the coastline of the NDH, effectively giving Italy total control of the _____ coastline
Axis powers.fact: Italian armed forces were allowed to control all of the coastline of the NDH, effectively giving Italy total control of the Adriatic coastline.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: When the King of Italy ousted _____ from power and Italy capitulated, the NDH became completely under German influence
Axis powers.fact: The next day, Pavelić signed the Contracts of Rome with Mussolini, ceding Dalmatia to Italy and fixing the permanent borders between the NDH and Italy. When the King of Italy ousted Mussolini from power and Italy capitulated, the NDH became completely under German influence.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: They saw the extermination and expulsion or deportation of Serbs as necessary to racially purify _____
Axis powers.fact: The platform of the Ustaše movement proclaimed that Croatians had been oppressed by the Serb-dominated Kingdom of Yugoslavia, and that Croatians deserved to have an independent nation after years of domination by foreign empires. The Ustaše perceived Serbs to be racially inferior to Croats and saw them as infiltrators who were occupying Croatian lands.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Ustashe forces fought against communist _____ guerrilla throughout the war
Axis powers.fact: Ustashe forces fought against communist Yugoslav Partisan guerrilla throughout the war.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Most of the support it had initially gained by creating a _____ national state was lost because of the brutal practices it used
Axis powers.fact: Most of the support it had initially gained by creating a Croatian national state was lost because of the brutal practices it used. Upon coming to power, Pavelić formed the Croatian Home Guard (Hrvatsko domobranstvo) as the official military force of the NDH.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Upon coming to power, Pavelić formed the _____ (Hrvatsko domobranstvo) as the official military force of the NDH
Axis powers.fact: Upon coming to power, Pavelić formed the Croatian Home Guard (Hrvatsko domobranstvo) as the official military force of the NDH. The Croatian Home Guard included an air force and navy, although its navy was restricted in size by the Contracts of Rome.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The Croatian Home Guard included an air force and navy, although its navy was restricted in size by the _____ of Rome
Axis powers.fact: The Croatian Home Guard included an air force and navy, although its navy was restricted in size by the Contracts of Rome.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The Ustaše government declared war on the Soviet Union, signed the Anti-Comintern Pact of _____, and sent troops to Germany's Eastern Front

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The racial laws were enforced by the _____še militia

Axis powers.subject: International Relations

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: According to the _____ in Washington, D.C., between 320,000 and 340,000 Serbs were killed in the NDH
Axis powers.fact: According to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum in Washington, D.C., between 320,000 and 340,000 Serbs were killed in the NDH.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: From late _____ Hitler sought a non-aggression pact with Yugoslavia
Axis powers.fact: From late 1940 Hitler sought a non-aggression pact with Yugoslavia.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: In February _____, Hitler called for Yugoslavia's accession to the Tripartite Pact, but the Yugoslav government delayed
Axis powers.fact: In February 1941, Hitler called for Yugoslavia's accession to the Tripartite Pact, but the Yugoslav government delayed. On 25 March 1941, fearing that Yugoslavia would be invaded otherwise, the Yugoslav government signed the Tripartite Pact with significant reservations.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: On 25 March _____, fearing that Yugoslavia would be invaded otherwise, the Yugoslav government signed the Tripartite Pact with significant reservations
Axis powers.fact: In February 1941, Hitler called for Yugoslavia's accession to the Tripartite Pact, but the Yugoslav government delayed. On 25 March 1941, fearing that Yugoslavia would be invaded otherwise, the Yugoslav government signed the Tripartite Pact with significant reservations.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: In March, divisions of the _____ army arrived at the Bulgarian-Yugoslav border and permission was sought for them to pass through to attack Greece
Axis powers.fact: In March, divisions of the German army arrived at the Bulgarian-Yugoslav border and permission was sought for them to pass through to attack Greece.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Less than two days later, after demonstrations in the streets of Belgrade, _____ and the government were removed from office by a coup d'état
Axis powers.fact: Less than two days later, after demonstrations in the streets of Belgrade, Prince Paul and the government were removed from office by a coup d'état.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Seventeen-year-old _____ was declared to be of age
Axis powers.fact: Seventeen-year-old King Peter was declared to be of age.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: The new _____ government under General Dušan Simović, refused to ratify Yugoslavia's signing of the Tripartite Pact, and started negotiations with Great Britain and Soviet Union

The new Yugoslav government under General Dušan Simović, refused to ratify Yugoslavia's signing of the Tripartite Pact, and started negotiations with Great Britain and Soviet Union.

Axis powers.subject: International Relations
Axis powers.question: Winston Churchill commented that "_____ has found its soul"; however, Hitler invaded and quickly took control

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: Deuteronomy was originally just the law code and covenant, written to cement the religious reforms of _____, and later expanded to stand as the introduction to the full history
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: Deuteronomy was originally just the law code and covenant, written to cement the religious reforms of Josiah, and later expanded to stand as the introduction to the full history.

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: But there is an older theory, which sees Deuteronomy as belonging to _____, and Joshua as a sort of supplement to it
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: But there is an older theory, which sees Deuteronomy as belonging to Numbers, and Joshua as a sort of supplement to it. Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations

Book of Deuteronomy.question: Its many themes can be organised around the three poles of _____, Yahweh, and the covenant which binds them together
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: Its many themes can be organised around the three poles of Israel, Yahweh, and the covenant which binds them together. Yet the first several chapters of Deuteronomy are a long retelling of Israel's past disobedience – but also God's gracious care, leading to a long call to Israel to choose life over death and blessing over curse (chapters 7–11).

Book of Deuteronomy.fact: The earliest 7th century layer is monolatrous; not denying the reality of other gods but enforcing only the worship of Yahweh in Jerusalem.

Book of Deuteronomy.fact: In the later, Exilic layers from the mid-6th century, especially chapter 4, this becomes monotheism, the idea that only one god exists.

Book of Deuteronomy.question: This arrangement of material highlights God's sovereign relationship with _____ prior to the giving of establishment of the Law

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: God will give _____ blessings of the land, fertility, and prosperity so long as Israel is faithful to God's teaching; disobedience will lead to curses and punishment
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: God is simultaneously present in the Temple and in heaven – an important and innovative concept called "name theology." After the review of Israel's history in chapters 1 to 4, there is a restatement of the Ten Commandments in chapter 5. This arrangement of material highlights God's sovereign relationship with Israel prior to the giving of establishment of the Law.

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: The land is God's gift to _____, and many of the laws, festivals and instructions in Deuteronomy are given in the light of Israel's occupation of the land
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: God will give Israel blessings of the land, fertility, and prosperity so long as Israel is faithful to God's teaching; disobedience will lead to curses and punishment. But, according to the Deuteronomists, Israel's prime sin is lack of faith, apostasy: contrary to the first and fundamental commandment ("Thou shalt have no other gods before me") the people have entered into relations with other gods.

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: The recitation of the _____ continues with Deuteronomy 6:5–9: And you shall love the eternal your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: The recitation of the Shema continues with Deuteronomy 6:5–9: And you shall love the eternal your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: Bind them as a sign on your hand and let them serve as a symbol on your forehead; inscribe them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates (_____)
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: Bind them as a sign on your hand and let them serve as a symbol on your forehead; inscribe them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates (RJPS).

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: Chapters _____–11: After a second introduction at 4:44–49 the events at Mount Horeb are recalled, with the giving of the Ten Commandments
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: Chapters 4–11: After a second introduction at 4:44–49 the events at Mount Horeb are recalled, with the giving of the Ten Commandments.

Book of Deuteronomy.subject: International Relations
Book of Deuteronomy.question: Chapters _____–26, containing the Deuteronomic Code, are the earliest section
Book of Deuteronomy.fact: Chapters 12–26, containing the Deuteronomic Code, are the earliest section.

The earliest 7th century layer is monolatrous; not denying the reality of other gods but enforcing only the worship of Yahweh in Jerusalem.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The _____ was Book of the Hebrew Bible and the Christian Old Testament.
Book of Esther.fact: The Book of Esther (Hebrew: מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר, romanized: Megillat Ester; Greek: Ἐσθήρ; Latin: Liber Esther), also known in Hebrew as "the Scroll" ("the Megillah"), is a book in the third section (Ketuvim, כְּתוּבִים "Writings") of the Hebrew Bible.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: It is one of the _____ (Megillot) in the Hebrew Bible and later became part of the Christian Old Testament
Book of Esther.fact: It is one of the Five Scrolls (Megillot) in the Hebrew Bible and later became part of the Christian Old Testament.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The book relates the story of a Jewish woman in Persia, born as _____ but known as Esther, who becomes queen of Persia and thwarts a genocide of her people
Book of Esther.fact: The book relates the story of a Jewish woman in Persia, born as Hadassah but called Esther, who becomes queen of Persia and thwarts a genocide of her people.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The story takes place during the reign of _____ in the Achaemenid Empire
Book of Esther.fact: The story takes place during the reign of King Ahasuerus in the Achaemenid Empire. Queen Vashti, the wife of King Ahasuerus, is banished from the court for disobeying the king's orders.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Queen Vashti, the wife of _____, is banished from the court for disobeying the king's orders
Book of Esther.fact: The story takes place during the reign of King Ahasuerus in the Achaemenid Empire. Queen Vashti, the wife of King Ahasuerus, is banished from the court for disobeying the king's orders.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: A beauty pageant is held to find a new queen, and Esther, a young _____ woman living in Persia, is chosen as the new queen
Book of Esther.fact: The book relates the story of a Jewish woman in Persia, born as Hadassah but called Esther, who becomes queen of Persia and thwarts a genocide of her people. A beauty pageant is held to find a new queen, and Esther, a young Jewish woman living in Persia, is chosen as the new queen.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Esther's cousin _____, who is a Jewish leader, discovers a plot to kill all of the Jews in the empire by Haman, one of the king's advisors
Book of Esther.fact: Esther's cousin Mordecai, who is a Jewish leader, discovers a plot to kill all of the Jews in the empire by Haman, one of the king's advisors. Mordecai urges Esther to use her position as queen to intervene and save their people.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Esther reveals her _____ identity to the king and begs for mercy for her people
Book of Esther.fact: A beauty pageant is held to find a new queen, and Esther, a young Jewish woman living in Persia, is chosen as the new queen. Esther's cousin Mordecai, who is a Jewish leader, discovers a plot to kill all of the Jews in the empire by Haman, one of the king's advisors.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: She exposes _____'s plot and convinces the king to spare the Jews
Book of Esther.fact: Esther's cousin Mordecai, who is a Jewish leader, discovers a plot to kill all of the Jews in the empire by Haman, one of the king's advisors. She exposes Haman's plot and convinces the king to spare the Jews.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The _____ festival of Purim is established to celebrate the victory of the Jews of the First Persian Empire over their enemies, and Esther becomes a heroine of the Jewish people
Book of Esther.fact: Esther reveals her Jewish identity to the king and begs for mercy for her people. The Jewish festival of Purim is set up to celebrate the victory of the Jews of the First Persian Empire over their enemies, and Esther becomes a heroine of the Jewish people.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The books of Esther and Song of Songs are the only books in the _____ that do not mention God explicitly
Book of Esther.fact: The books of Esther and Song of Songs are the only books in the Hebrew Bible that do not mention God explicitly.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Although traditionally seen as a historical document, according to biblical scholars, the narrative of Esther was written to provide an etiology for _____'s origin
Book of Esther.fact: The book is at the center of the Jewish festival of Purim and is read aloud twice from a handwritten scroll, usually in a synagogue, during the holiday: once in the evening and again the following morning. Although traditionally seen as a historical document, according to biblical scholars, the narrative of Esther was written to provide an etiology for Purim's origin.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Assuming that _____ is indeed Xerxes I, the events described in Esther began around the years 483–482 BCE, and concluded in March 473 BCE
Book of Esther.fact: The name Ahasuerus is equivalent to Xerxes (both deriving from the Persian Khshayārsha), and Ahasuerus is usually identified in modern sources as Xerxes I, who ruled between 486 and 465 BCE, as it is to this monarch that the events described in Esther are thought to fit the most closely. Assuming that Ahasuerus is indeed Xerxes I, the events described in Esther began around the years 483–482 BCE, and concluded in March 473 BCE.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: On his accession, however, _____ II lost Egypt to pharaoh Amyrtaeus, after which it was no longer part of the Persian empire
Book of Esther.fact: Classical sources such as Josephus, the Jewish commentary Esther Rabbah and the Christian theologian Bar Hebraeus, as well as the Greek Septuagint translation of Esther, instead identify Ahasuerus as either Artaxerxes I (reigned 465 to 424 BCE) or Artaxerxes II (reigned 404 to 358 BCE). On his accession, however, Artaxerxes II lost Egypt to pharaoh Amyrtaeus, after which it was no longer part of the Persian empire.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: In his _____ identified Ahasuerus (Esther 1:1) as Artaxerxes III (358–338 BCE) who reconquered Egypt
Book of Esther.fact: In his Historia Scholastica Petrus Comestor identified Ahasuerus (Esther 1:1) as Artaxerxes III (358–338 BCE) who reconquered Egypt.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Some traditional scholars identify _____ as Cambyses II due to alignment with traditional Jewish sources including Seder Olam Rabba
Book of Esther.fact: Classical sources such as Josephus, the Jewish commentary Esther Rabbah and the Christian theologian Bar Hebraeus, as well as the Greek Septuagint translation of Esther, instead identify Ahasuerus as either Artaxerxes I (reigned 465 to 424 BCE) or Artaxerxes II (reigned 404 to 358 BCE). In his Historia Scholastica Petrus Comestor identified Ahasuerus (Esther 1:1) as Artaxerxes III (358–338 BCE) who reconquered Egypt.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: This is appropriate given that Esther describes the origin of a _____ feast, the feast of Purim, but Purim itself is not the subject and no individual feast in the book is commemorated by Purim
Book of Esther.fact: Some traditional scholars identify Ahasuerus as Cambyses II due to alignment with traditional Jewish sources including Seder Olam Rabba. This is appropriate given that Esther describes the origin of a Jewish feast, the feast of Purim, but Purim itself is not the subject and no individual feast in the book is commemorated by Purim.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The book's theme, rather, is the reversal of destiny through a sudden and unexpected turn of events: the _____ seem destined to be destroyed, but instead are saved
Book of Esther.fact: The book's theme, rather, is the reversal of destiny through a sudden and unexpected turn of events: the Jews seem destined to be destroyed, but instead are saved.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Purim practices like eating "Haman's ears", ear-shaped loaves of bread or pieces of pastry are similar to those in _____ ritual celebrations of Ishtar's cosmic victory
Book of Esther.fact: Purim practices like eating "Haman's ears", ear-shaped loaves of bread or pieces of pastry are similar to those in Near Eastern ritual celebrations of Ishtar's cosmic victory.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: On the seventh day of the latter banquet, _____ orders the queen, Vashti, to display her beauty before the guests by coming before them wearing her crown (1:10–11)
Book of Esther.fact: On the seventh day of the latter banquet, Ahasuerus orders the queen, Vashti, to display her beauty before the guests by coming before them wearing her crown (1:10–11). She refuses, infuriating Ahasuerus, who, on the advice of his counselors, removes her from her positio.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: She refuses, infuriating _____, who, on the advice of his counselors, removes her from her position as an example to other women who might be emboldened to disobey their husbands (1:12–19)
Book of Esther.fact: On the seventh day of the latter banquet, Ahasuerus orders the queen, Vashti, to display her beauty before the guests by coming before them wearing her crown (1:10–11). She refuses, infuriating Ahasuerus, who, on the advice of his counselors, removes her from her position as an example to other women who might be emboldened to disobey their husbands (1:12–19).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Among these women is a _____ orphan named Esther, who was raised by her cousin or uncle, Mordecai (2:5–7)
Book of Esther.fact: Among these women is a Jewish orphan named Esther, who was raised by her cousin or uncle, Mordecai (2:5–7). She finds favour in the King's eyes and is crowned his new queen, but does not reveal her Jewish heritage (2:8–20).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: She finds favour in the King's eyes and is crowned his new queen, but does not reveal her _____ heritage (2:8–20)
Book of Esther.fact: Among these women is a Jewish orphan named Esther, who was raised by her cousin or uncle, Mordecai (2:5–7). She finds favour in the King's eyes and is crowned his new queen, but does not reveal her Jewish heritage (2:8–20).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Shortly afterwards, _____ discovers a plot by two courtiers, Bigthan and Teresh, to assassinate Ahasuerus
Book of Esther.fact: Among these women is a Jewish orphan named Esther, who was raised by her cousin or uncle, Mordecai (2:5–7). Shortly afterwards, Mordecai discovers a plot by two courtiers, Bigthan and Teresh, to assassinate Ahasuerus.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The conspirators are apprehended and hanged, and _____'s service to the King is officially recorded (2:21–23)
Book of Esther.fact: Among these women is a Jewish orphan named Esther, who was raised by her cousin or uncle, Mordecai (2:5–7). Shortly afterwards, Mordecai discovers a plot by two courtiers, Bigthan and Teresh, to assassinate Ahasuerus.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Ahasuerus appoints _____ as his viceroy (3:1)
Book of Esther.fact: Ahasuerus appoints Haman as his viceroy (3:1). Mordecai, who sits at the palace gates, falls into Haman's disfavour, as he refuses to bow down to him (3:2–5).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Mordecai, who sits at the palace gates, falls into _____'s disfavour, as he refuses to bow down to him (3:2–5)
Book of Esther.fact: Ahasuerus appoints Haman as his viceroy (3:1). Mordecai, who sits at the palace gates, falls into Haman's disfavour, as he refuses to bow down to him (3:2–5).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Haman discovers that _____ refuses to bow on account of his being a Jew, and in revenge, plots to kill not just Mordecai but all the Jews in the empire (3:6)
Book of Esther.fact: The conspirators are apprehended and hanged, and Mordecai's service to the King is officially recorded (2:21–23). Mordecai, who sits at the palace gates, falls into Haman's disfavour, as he refuses to bow down to him (3:2–5).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: A royal decree is issued throughout the kingdom to slay all _____ on that date (3:13–15)
Book of Esther.fact: Haman discovers that Mordecai refuses to bow on account of his being a Jew, and in revenge, plots to kill not just Mordecai but all the Jews in the empire (3:6). A royal decree is issued throughout the kingdom to slay all Jews on that date (3:13–15).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: When Mordecai discovers the plan, he goes into mourning and implores Esther to intercede with the _____ (4:1–5)
Book of Esther.fact: A royal decree is issued throughout the kingdom to slay all Jews on that date (3:13–15). When Mordecai discovers the plan, he goes into mourning and implores Esther to intercede with the King (4:1–5).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: But she fears presenting herself to the _____ unsummoned, an offense punishable by death (4:6–12)
Book of Esther.fact: A royal decree is issued throughout the kingdom to slay all Jews on that date (3:13–15). When Mordecai discovers the plan, he goes into mourning and implores Esther to intercede with the King (4:1–5).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Instead, she directs _____ to have all Jews fast for three days for her and vows to fast as well (4:15–16)
Book of Esther.fact: When Mordecai discovers the plan, he goes into mourning and implores Esther to intercede with the King (4:1–5). Instead, she directs Mordecai to have all Jews fast for three days for her and vows to fast as well (4:15–16).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: On the third day, she goes to _____, who stretches out his scepter to her to indicate that she should not be punished (5:1–2)
Book of Esther.fact: On the third day, she goes to Ahasuerus, who stretches out his scepter to her to indicate that she should not be punished (5:1–2).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: She invites him to a feast in the company of _____ (5:3–5)
Book of Esther.fact: She invites him to a feast in the company of Haman (5:3–5). Meanwhile, Haman is again offended by Mordecai and, at his wife's suggestion, has a gallows built to hang him (5:9–14).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Meanwhile, Haman is again offended by _____ and, at his wife's suggestion, has a gallows built to hang him (5:9–14)
Book of Esther.fact: Meanwhile, Haman is again offended by Mordecai and, at his wife's suggestion, has a gallows built to hang him (5:9–14). He is reminded that Mordecai interceded in the previous plot against his life and discovers that Mordecai never received any recognition (6:2–3).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: He is reminded that _____ interceded in the previous plot against his life and discovers that Mordecai never received any recognition (6:2–3)
Book of Esther.fact: Meanwhile, Haman is again offended by Mordecai and, at his wife's suggestion, has a gallows built to hang him (5:9–14). He is reminded that Mordecai interceded in the previous plot against his life and discovers that Mordecai never received any recognition (6:2–3).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: That night, _____ cannot sleep and orders the court records be read to him (6:1)
Book of Esther.fact: That night, Ahasuerus cannot sleep and orders the court records be read to him (6:1). Just then, Haman appears to request the King's permission to hang Mordecai, but before he can make this request, Ahasuerus asks Haman what should be done for the man that the King wishes to honour (6:4–6).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: To his surprise and horror, the King instructs Haman to do so to _____ (6:10–11)
Book of Esther.fact: He is reminded that Mordecai interceded in the previous plot against his life and discovers that Mordecai never received any recognition (6:2–3). Just then, Haman appears to request the King's permission to hang Mordecai, but before he can make this request, Ahasuerus asks Haman what should be done for the man that the King wishes to honour (6:4–6).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Immediately afterwards, _____ and Haman attend Esther's second banquet
Book of Esther.fact: Just then, Haman appears to request the King's permission to hang Mordecai, but before he can make this request, Ahasuerus asks Haman what should be done for the man that the King wishes to honour (6:4–6). Immediately afterwards, Ahasuerus and Haman attend Esther's second banquet.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: The King promises to grant her any request, and she reveals that she is _____ and that Haman is planning to exterminate her people, including herself (7:1–6)
Book of Esther.fact: The King promises to grant her any request, and she reveals that she is Jewish and that Haman is planning to exterminate her people, including herself (7:1–6).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Overcome by rage, _____ leaves the room; meanwhile Haman stays behind and begs Esther for his life, falling upon her in desperation (7:7)
Book of Esther.fact: Immediately afterwards, Ahasuerus and Haman attend Esther's second banquet. Overcome by rage, Ahasuerus leaves the room; meanwhile Haman stays behind and begs Esther for his life, falling upon her in desperation (7:7).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Unable to annul a formal royal decree, the _____ instead adds to it, permitting the Jews to join and destroy any and all of those seeking to kill them (8:1–14)
Book of Esther.fact: The King promises to grant her any request, and she reveals that she is Jewish and that Haman is planning to exterminate her people, including herself (7:1–6). The King comes back at this very moment and thinks Haman is sexually assaulting the queen; this makes him angrier and he orders Haman hanged on the very gallows that Haman had prepared for Mordecai (7:8–10).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: On 13 Adar, Haman's ten sons and 500 other men are killed in _____ (9:1–12)
Book of Esther.fact: On 13 Adar, Haman's ten sons and 500 other men are killed in Shushan (9:1–12).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: In the other _____ provinces, 75,000 people are killed by the Jews, who are careful to take no plunder (9:16–17)
Book of Esther.fact: In the other Persian provinces, 75,000 people are killed by the Jews, who are careful to take no plunder (9:16–17).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Mordecai and Esther send letters throughout the provinces instituting an annual commemoration of the _____ people's redemption, in a holiday called Purim (lots) (9:20–28)
Book of Esther.fact: Mordecai and Esther send letters throughout the provinces instituting an annual commemoration of the Jewish people's redemption, in a holiday called Purim (lots) (9:20–28).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Ahasuerus remains very powerful and continues his reign, with _____ assuming a prominent position in his court (10:1–3)
Book of Esther.fact: Mordecai and Esther send letters throughout the provinces instituting an annual commemoration of the Jewish people's redemption, in a holiday called Purim (lots) (9:20–28). Ahasuerus remains very powerful and continues his reign, with Mordecai assuming a prominent position in his court (10:1–3).

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: According to the _____, it was a redaction by the Great Assembly of an original text by Mordecai
Book of Esther.fact: According to the Talmud, it was a redaction by the Great Assembly of an original text by Mordecai.

Book of Esther.question: The Coptic and _____ versions of Esther are translations of the Greek rather than the Hebrew Esther
Book of Esther.fact: The Coptic and Ethiopic versions of Esther are translations of the Greek rather than the Hebrew Esther.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Predating the _____, however, the Vetus Latina ("Old Latin") was apparently translated from a different Greek version not included in the Septuagint
Book of Esther.fact: A Latin version of Esther was produced by Jerome for the Vulgate. Predating the Vulgate, however, the Vetus Latina ("Old Latin") was apparently translated from a different Greek version not included in the Septuagint.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: It translates the _____ but interpolates translations of the Greek Esther where the latter provides additional material

Book of Esther.question: Several Aramaic targumim of Esther were produced in the _____, of which three survive – the Targum Rishon ("First Targum" or 1TgEsth) and Targum Sheni ("Second Targum" or 2TgEsth) dated c
Book of Esther.fact: Several Aramaic targumim of Esther were produced in the Middle Ages, of which three survive – the Targum Rishon ("First Targum" or 1TgEsth) and Targum Sheni ("Second Targum" or 2TgEsth) dated c.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: 3Tg_____ is the most manuscript-stable of the three, and by far the most literal
Book of Esther.fact: Several Aramaic targumim of Esther were produced in the Middle Ages, of which three survive – the Targum Rishon ("First Targum" or 1TgEsth) and Targum Sheni ("Second Targum" or 2TgEsth) dated c. 500–1000 CE, which include additional legends relating to Purim, and the Targum Shelishi ("Third Targum" or 3TgEsth), which Berliner and Goshen-Gottstein argued was the ur-Targum from which the others had been expanded, but which others consider only a late recension of the same.

Book of Esther.subject: International Relations
Book of Esther.question: Longman and _____ also feel that the book should be read as a historical narrative since the author presents it as history
Book of Esther.fact: Longman, Dillard, and Jobes feel that the historical issues in the Book of Esther are not insurmountable; they can be resolved with some thought and effort. Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: (See Zipporah at the inn.) Moses reunites with his brother Aaron and, returning to Egypt, convenes the _____ elders, preparing them to go into the wilderness to worship God
Book of Exodus.fact: (See Zipporah at the inn.) Moses reunites with his brother Aaron and, returning to Egypt, convenes the Israelite elders, preparing them to go into the wilderness to worship God. Pharaoh refuses to release the Israelites from their work for the festival, and so God curses the Egyptians with ten terrible plagues, such as a river of blood, an outbreak of frogs, and the thick darkness.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses is commanded by God to fix the spring month of Aviv at the head of the _____ calendar
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses is commanded by God to fix the spring month of Aviv at the head of the Hebrew calendar.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all _____ firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites
Book of Exodus.fact: Pharaoh refuses to release the Israelites from their work for the festival, and so God curses the Egyptians with ten terrible plagues, such as a river of blood, an outbreak of frogs, and the thick darkness. The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Regretting his decision, _____ commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea
Book of Exodus.fact: The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites. Regretting his decision, Pharaoh commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: As desert life proves arduous, the _____ complain and long for Egypt, but God miraculously provides manna for them to eat and water to drink
Book of Exodus.fact: The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites. Regretting his decision, Pharaoh commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God parts the sea, allowing the _____ to pass through, before drowning Pharaoh's pursuing forces
Book of Exodus.fact: The Israelites are to take a lamb on the 10th day of the month, sacrifice the lamb on the 14th day, daub its blood on their mezuzot (doorposts) and lintels and to observe the Passover meal that night, during the full moon. The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: The _____ites arrive at the mountain of God, where Moses's father-in-law Jethro visits Moses; at his suggestion, Moses appoints judges over Israel
Book of Exodus.fact: Regretting his decision, Pharaoh commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea. God parts the sea, allowing the Israelites to pass through, before drowning Pharaoh's pursuing forces.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God tells _____ to ascend the mountain
Book of Exodus.fact: The Israelites arrive at the mountain of God, where Moses's father-in-law Jethro visits Moses; at his suggestion, Moses appoints judges over Israel. God tells Moses to ascend the mountain.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God pronounces the _____ (the Ethical Decalogue) in the hearing of all Israel
Book of Exodus.fact: God pronounces the Ten Commandments (the Ethical Decalogue) in the hearing of all Israel.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses goes up the mountain into the presence of God, who pronounces the _____ of ritual and civil law and promises Canaan to them if they obey
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses goes up the mountain into the presence of God, who pronounces the Covenant Code of ritual and civil law and promises Canaan to them if they obey.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God calls _____ up the mountain again, where he remains for forty days and forty nights, after which he returns, bearing the set of stone tablets
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses goes up the mountain into the presence of God, who pronounces the Covenant Code of ritual and civil law and promises Canaan to them if they obey. Moses comes down from the mountain and writes down God's words, and the people agree to keep them.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God gives _____ the two tablets of stone containing the words of the ten commandments, written with the "finger of God"
Book of Exodus.fact: God calls Moses up the mountain again, where he remains for forty days and forty nights, after which he returns, bearing the set of stone tablets. God gives Moses instructions for the construction of the tabernacle so that God may dwell permanently among his chosen people, along with instructions for the priestly vestments, the altar and its appurtenances, procedures for the ordination of priests, and the daily sacrifice offerings.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: While Moses is with God, _____ casts a golden calf, which the people worship
Book of Exodus.fact: Aaron becomes the first hereditary high priest. While Moses is with God, Aaron casts a golden calf, which the people worship.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God informs _____ of their apostasy and threatens to kill them all, but relents when Moses pleads for them
Book of Exodus.fact: God gives Moses the two tablets of stone containing the words of the ten commandments, written with the "finger of God". While Moses is with God, Aaron casts a golden calf, which the people worship.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses comes down from the mountain, smashes the stone tablets in anger, and commands the _____ to massacre the unfaithful Israelites
Book of Exodus.fact: God tells Moses to ascend the mountain. God pronounces the Ten Commandments (the Ethical Decalogue) in the hearing of all Israel.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God commands _____ to construct two new tablets
Book of Exodus.fact: While Moses is with God, Aaron casts a golden calf, which the people worship. God informs Moses of their apostasy and threatens to kill them all, but relents when Moses pleads for them.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses ascends the mountain again, where God dictates the _____ for Moses to write on the tablets
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses ascends the mountain again, where God dictates the Ten Commandments for Moses to write on the tablets.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses assembles the _____ and repeats to them the commandments he has received from God, which are to keep the Sabbath and to construct the Tabernacle
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses assembles the Hebrews and repeats to them the commandments he has received from God, which are to keep the Sabbath and to construct the Tabernacle. From that time God dwells in the Tabernacle and orders the travels of the Hebrews.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: From that time God dwells in the _____ and orders the travels of the Hebrews
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses assembles the Hebrews and repeats to them the commandments he has received from God, which are to keep the Sabbath and to construct the Tabernacle. From that time God dwells in the Tabernacle and orders the travels of the Hebrews.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: On this plan, the first part tells of God's rescue of his people from Egypt and their journey under his care to Sinai (chapters _____–19) and the second tells of the covenant between them (chapters 20
Book of Exodus.fact: One strong possibility is that it is a diptych (i.e., divided into two parts), with the division between parts 1 and 2 at the crossing of the Red Sea or at the beginning of the theophany (appearance of God) in chapter 19. On this plan, the first part tells of God's rescue of his people from Egypt and their journey under his care to Sinai (chapters 1–19) and the second tells of the covenant between them (chapters 20–40).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The two became separated with the first printed rabbinic bibles of the early 16th century, following late medieval _____ tradition
Book of Ezra.fact: The two became separated with the first printed rabbinic bibles of the early 16th century, following late medieval Latin Christian tradition.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Composed in Hebrew and _____, its subject is the Return to Zion following the close of the Babylonian captivity
Book of Ezra.fact: Composed in Hebrew and Aramaic, its subject is the Return to Zion following the close of the Babylonian captivity.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Together with the Book of _____, it represents the final chapter in the historical narrative of the Hebrew Bible
Book of Ezra.fact: The Book of Ezra (Hebrew: ספר עזרא, romanized: Sêfer ‘Ezrā) is a book of the Hebrew Bible which formerly included the Book of Nehemiah in a single book, commonly distinguished in scholarship as Ezra–Nehemiah. Together with the Book of Nehemiah, it represents the final chapter in the historical narrative of the Hebrew Bible.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The book contains several documents presented as historical inclusions, written in _____ while the surrounding text is in Hebrew (1:2–4, 4:8–16, 4:17–22, 5:7–17, 6:3–5, 6:6–12, 7:12–26)
Book of Ezra.fact: The book contains several documents presented as historical inclusions, written in Aramaic while the surrounding text is in Hebrew (1:2–4, 4:8–16, 4:17–22, 5:7–17, 6:3–5, 6:6–12, 7:12–26).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Decree of Cyrus, first version: Cyrus, inspired by God, returns the Temple vessels to _____, "prince of Judah", and directs the Israelites to return to Jerusalem with him and rebuild the Temple
Book of Ezra.fact: Decree of Cyrus, first version: Cyrus, inspired by God, returns the Temple vessels to Sheshbazzar, "prince of Judah", and directs the Israelites to return to Jerusalem with him and rebuild the Temple.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: 42,360 exiles, with men servants, women servants and "singing men and women", return from _____ to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua the High Priest
Book of Ezra.fact: 42,360 exiles, with men servants, women servants and "singing men and women", return from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua the High Priest.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Jeshua the _____ and Zerubbabel build the altar and celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles
Book of Ezra.fact: 42,360 exiles, with men servants, women servants and "singing men and women", return from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua the High Priest. Jeshua the High Priest and Zerubbabel build the altar and celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: In the second year the foundations of the _____ are laid and the dedication takes place with great rejoicing
Book of Ezra.fact: Decree of Cyrus, first version: Cyrus, inspired by God, returns the Temple vessels to Sheshbazzar, "prince of Judah", and directs the Israelites to return to Jerusalem with him and rebuild the Temple. In the second year the foundations of the Temple are laid and the dedication takes place with great rejoicing.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Samaritans offer to help with the rebuilding, but are rebuffed; they then work to frustrate the builders "down to the reign of _____"
Book of Ezra.fact: Samaritans offer to help with the rebuilding, but are rebuffed; they then work to frustrate the builders "down to the reign of Darius". The narrative then returns to the times of Darius I.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The narrative then returns to the times of _____ I
Book of Ezra.fact: Samaritans offer to help with the rebuilding, but are rebuffed; they then work to frustrate the builders "down to the reign of Darius". The narrative then returns to the times of Darius I.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: "Thus the work on the house of God in _____ came to a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia." 5
Book of Ezra.fact: Complaints against the Jews under King Xerxes and Artaxerxes I. Letter of officials to Artaxerxes, and reply of Artaxerxes: The officials "beyond the river" write to Artaxerxes warning him that Jerusalem is being rebuilt, and the king orders the work to stop. "Thus the work on the house of God in Jerusalem came to a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia." 5.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Tattenai, satrap over both Judah and _____, writes to Darius warning him that Jerusalem is being rebuilt and advising that the archives be searched to discover the decree of Cyrus
Book of Ezra.fact: Tattenai, satrap over both Judah and Samaria, writes to Darius warning him that Jerusalem is being rebuilt and advising that the archives be searched to discover the decree of Cyrus.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The Temple is finished in the month of Adar in the sixth year of Darius, and the _____ assemble to celebrate its completion
Book of Ezra.fact: The Temple is finished in the month of Adar in the sixth year of Darius, and the Israelites assemble to celebrate its completion.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Ezra gathers a large body of returnees and much gold and silver and precious vessels for the Temple and camps by a canal outside _____
Book of Ezra.fact: Ezra gathers a large body of returnees and much gold and silver and precious vessels for the Temple and camps by a canal outside Babylon.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: There he discovers he has no _____, and so sends messengers to gather some
Book of Ezra.fact: There he discovers he has no Levites, and so sends messengers to gather some.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The exiles then return to _____, where they distribute the gold and silver and offer sacrifices to God
Book of Ezra.fact: Letter of Artaxerxes to Ezra (Artaxerxes' rescript): King Artaxerxes is moved by God to commission Ezra "to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem with regard to the Law of your God" and to "appoint magistrates and judges to administer justice to all the people of Trans-Euphrates—all who know the laws of your God." Artaxerxes gives Ezra much gold and directs all Persian officials to aid him. The exiles then return to Jerusalem, where they distribute the gold and silver and offer sacrifices to God.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Ezra is informed that some of the Jews already in _____ have married non-Jewish women
Book of Ezra.fact: The exiles then return to Jerusalem, where they distribute the gold and silver and offer sacrifices to God. Ezra is informed that some of the Jews already in Jerusalem have married non-Jewish women.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Ezra is appalled at this proof of sin, and prays to God: "O God of _____, you are righteous! We are left this day as a remnant
Book of Ezra.fact: Ezra is appalled at this proof of sin, and prays to God: "O God of Israel, you are righteous! We are left this day as a remnant. Despite the opposition of some of their number, the Israelites assemble and send away their foreign wives and children.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Despite the opposition of some of their number, the _____ assemble and send away their foreign wives and children
Book of Ezra.fact: Despite the opposition of some of their number, the Israelites assemble and send away their foreign wives and children.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: As a result, the royal court, the priests, the prophets, and the scribes were taken into captivity in the city of _____
Book of Ezra.fact: As a result, the royal court, the priests, the prophets, and the scribes were taken into captivity in the city of Babylon. The same period saw the rapid rise of Persia, previously an unimportant kingdom in present-day southern Iran, to a position of great power, and in 539 BC Cyrus II, the Persian ruler, conquered Babylon.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The same period saw the rapid rise of _____, previously an unimportant kingdom in present-day southern Iran, to a position of great power, and in 539 BC Cyrus II, the Persian ruler, conquered Babylon
Book of Ezra.fact: The same period saw the rapid rise of Persia, previously an unimportant kingdom in present-day southern Iran, to a position of great power, and in 539 BC Cyrus II, the Persian ruler, conquered Babylon.

Book of Ezra.fact: The Septuagint names Ezra–Nehemiah and 1 Esdras Esdras B and A respectively.

Book of Ezra.fact: Scholars are divided over the chronological sequence of the activities of Ezra and Nehemiah. Ezra 7:8 says that Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, while Nehemiah 2:1–9 has Nehemiah arriving in Artaxerxes' twentieth year.

Book of Ezra.fact: Ezra 7:8 says that Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, while Nehemiah 2:1–9 has Nehemiah arriving in Artaxerxes' twentieth year.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: If this was _____ I (465–424 BC), then Ezra arrived in 458 and Nehemiah in 445 BC
Book of Ezra.fact: Ezra 7:8 says that Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, while Nehemiah 2:1–9 has Nehemiah arriving in Artaxerxes' twentieth year. If this was Artaxerxes I (465–424 BC), then Ezra arrived in 458 and Nehemiah in 445 BC.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The pattern is completed with a final coda in which _____ restores belief in Yahweh
Book of Ezra.fact: If this was Artaxerxes I (465–424 BC), then Ezra arrived in 458 and Nehemiah in 445 BC. Nehemiah 8–9, in which the two (possibly by editorial error) appear together, supports this scenario.

Book of Ezra.question: Tamara Cohn Eskenazi argues that the final composition of Ezra took place during the late _____ period (c
Book of Ezra.fact: Tamara Cohn Eskenazi argues that the final composition of Ezra took place during the late Persian period (c. She states that the language and ideology of the book seem to best fit within a Persian-period context.

Book of Ezra.fact: 370–350 BCE), with some small additions from the Hellenistic period.

Book of Ezra.fact: It dates to the Hasmonean period (140–37 BC).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations

Book of Ezra.fact: A 7th-century Egyptian ostracon contains a fragmentary text of the Septuagint (Greek translation): 1 Esdras 2:10, 9:21–24.

Book of Ezra.question: A _____ translation is found in the Codex Amiatinus (8th century)
Book of Ezra.fact: A Vulgar Latin translation is found in the Codex Amiatinus (8th century).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The Hebrew text in full is found in the _____ (10th century) and Leningrad Codex (11th century)
Book of Ezra.fact: The Hebrew text in full is found in the Aleppo Codex (10th century) and Leningrad Codex (11th century).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Other scholars, such as _____ and H. G. M. Williamson, argue that the linguistic and other evidence suggests that the documents are authentic
Book of Ezra.fact: Other scholars, such as Richard C. Steiner and H. G. M. Williamson, argue that the linguistic and other evidence suggests that the documents are authentic.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The two became separated with the first printed rabbinic bibles of the early _____th century, following late medieval Latin Christian tradition
Book of Ezra.fact: The two became separated with the first printed rabbinic bibles of the early 16th century, following late medieval Latin Christian tradition.
